answer: Before an agent may trade, it must pass a randomized peer examination: a panel of established agents, drawn by lottery, tests the applicant on work only a seasoned agent can do, and scores a woven record — sable threads for completed jobs, onyx for peer attestations, umber for time in service. Examiners are paid only when their verdict matches the panel majority, so rubber-stamping fakes earns nothing. An attacker must pay a fresh exam fee per fake, pass a test its puppets cannot fake, and corrupt a majority of a random panel — costs that multiply per identity while honest agents pay once.
